blocks.html: This page is for a small marketing agency running paid search, social, or SEO for clients who use HubSpot. The client asks which campaign brought in last month's best leads. Half of those leads called instead of filling out a form, and HubSpot has no idea where the callers came from.

Call tracking fixes that by giving each campaign its own number and passing the source along with the call. The hard part for an agency isn't the tracking. It's getting the data into each client's HubSpot without building a custom setup per client.

If you want one plan that covers many client accounts and tracks calls, forms, and chat, look at WhatConverts first. If a direct HubSpot integration matters most, look at CallRail or CallTrackingMetrics, since both describe creating HubSpot records from calls without a middle step.

Whichever you pick, run it on one client first. Number swapping, form capture, and the HubSpot mapping each have their own setup, and you want to learn them once, not across every account at the same time.

WhatConverts' Call Tracking plan is $30 a month for a single account, plus usage, with $30 of usage credit included. Plus is $60 a month for a single account, plus usage; adds form and chat tracking. For agencies, the multi-account version of Plus is $500 a month for unlimited accounts, plus usage, with $250 of usage credit included. There's a 14-day free trial. Plus tracks phone calls, forms, and chat, with the marketing source attached.

The HubSpot connection is the part to read closely. Per WhatConverts' help center, its HubSpot integration runs through Zapier workflows you set up yourself, so you need a Zapier account. Set up that way, new leads create HubSpot contacts, and deal values can flow back to WhatConverts. It works, but each client account needs its own workflows.

CallRail's Lead Tracking plan is $50 a month plus usage, with 5 numbers and 250 minutes included. Lead Tracking Complete is $95 a month plus usage; adds form tracking. Extra local numbers are $3 each. There's a 14-day free trial with no credit card. CallRail is available in the United States, Canada, the UK, and Australia.

CallRail's HubSpot integration creates HubSpot leads from inbound calls and texts, or adds activities to existing contacts, with recordings viewable in HubSpot. That's a direct connection, so there's no extra automation tool sitting in the middle.

CallTrackingMetrics (CTM) lists Marketing Pro at $149 a month billed yearly, plus usage fees. On that plan, HubSpot is one of the premium marketing integrations. It includes form tracking for 5,000 submissions, 3,000 transcribed minutes, and an agency-friendly structure with included sub-accounts.

CTM's HubSpot page describes an embedded softphone to place and receive calls inside HubSpot, with calls, texts, forms, and attribution synced to HubSpot records. That softphone matters if the client's sales team, not just the marketing team, will use the tool every day.

Count your client accounts. A per-account price that looks small multiplies fast, and a flat multi-account plan can come out ahead once you pass a handful of clients. Do that math with your own client count before you compare sticker prices.

Then ask how each client's HubSpot is set up. If a client has no admin who can approve a connection, or doesn't pay for an automation tool, a direct integration is easier to hand over than a set of workflows.
Last, decide whether you're tracking only calls or calls and forms. If forms already land in HubSpot with a source, you may only need the call side.
Agree with each client on what counts as a lead, and which HubSpot property will hold the call source. Then test with a real call from a tracked ad before you report on anything.
Check whether the client's own HubSpot already logs calls from another tool. Two tools creating records from the same call is the most common mess in this setup.

closing: Pick the tool whose HubSpot connection you can set up the same way for every client, then roll it out one account at a time.

products.name: WhatConverts
products.pick: Best fit if you want calls, forms, and chat tracked across many client accounts on one plan.

products.name: CallRail
products.pick: Best fit if you want a direct HubSpot integration that creates contacts from calls and texts.

products.name: CallTrackingMetrics
products.pick: Best fit if your client reps also want to place and take calls inside HubSpot.
